metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: does a repeatable, domain-specific Claude capability like client-report mean Claude has a built-in finance app or hidden logic for the task, or is it just a plain-text file of instructions Claude reads and follows? beats.narration_text: Someone assumed Claude's client-report capability was a built-in finance app. It isn't — it's a plain-text skill Claude reads. So: does Claude's client-report skill understand finance, or does it just follow steps?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 1.0 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('app' -> 'skill') lands on screen and the full corrected question finishes typing before the clip ends. Text/rates chosen from the established hai-simple fix pattern (42ms/char, 4% mistakeRate, 8% hesitateBetween, 4-line/64-char text) after the agent-development sibling's first-attempt timeout at slower/higher rates.

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is client-report. The SKILL.md file holds the full instruction set — plain language, no hidden code. Claude reads it, then acts. The file is the program.
The pipeline lives in the file's Steps section. Claude reads the file, runs each step in order, and returns the result — linear, no branching unless a step itself says so.

Client-report's SKILL.md spells out exactly what to produce: portfolio returns, an allocation breakdown, market commentary, timed for quarterly or annual delivery. Feed it the same numbers twice, and it builds the same report twice. Ask for something the file doesn't cover — a chart type it never mentions, a client segment it doesn't list — and there's no instruction to fall back on, so Claude reasons past the file on its own.

beats.narration_text: A Claude skill isn't a hidden app — it's a plain-text file of instructions, so the same input produces the same report every time. Whatever that file doesn't say, Claude has to work out on its own.

props.quote: A Claude skill isn't a hidden app — it's a plain-text file of instructions, so the same input produces the same report every time. Whatever that file doesn't say, Claude has to work out on its own.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: write a SKILL.md for a report I create regularly. List exactly what must appear every time, then list what would be left to my judgment because the file doesn't cover it. Read back what Claude wrote — the first list is what repeats identically every run; the second is where it's reasoning past the file, not following it.
